grades.reason: This is a LoongArch table of contents with timer CSR section titles. It says nothing about RISC-V mtime/mtimecmp, so it is the wrong ISA and has no content.

grades.quote: Bits `mip` .MTIP and `mie` .MTIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for machine timer interrupts. MTIP is read-only in the `mip` register, and is cleared by writing to the memory-mapped machine-mode timer compare register.
grades.reason: It describes the RISC-V MTIP/MTIE bits. MTIP is read-only in mip and is cleared by writing the memory-mapped timer compare register. That covers the clearing condition and the MTIE enable. It does not say that mtime >= mtimecmp sets MTIP.

grades.quote: Multiple simultaneous interrupts destined for M-mode are handled in the following decreasing priority order: MEI, MSI, MTI, SEI, SSI, STI, LCOFI.
grades.reason: It covers the rest of mip/mie, mostly supervisor interrupts and priority. It places the machine timer interrupt (MTI) in the priority order. It does not explain how mtime/mtimecmp set or clear the interrupt, so it is only marginally useful.

grades.quote: A machine timer interrupt becomes pending whenever `mtime` contains a value greater than or equal to `mtimecmp` , treating the values as unsigned integers. The interrupt remains posted until `mtimecmp` becomes greater than `mtime` (typically as a result of writing `mtimecmp` ). The interrupt will only be taken if interrupts are enabled and the MTIE bit is set in the `mie` register.
grades.reason: It directly explains the mechanism. The machine timer interrupt becomes pending when mtime >= mtimecmp (unsigned). It stays pending until mtimecmp becomes greater than mtime, usually by writing mtimecmp. It is taken only if interrupts are enabled and MTIE is set. It also notes that MTIP may lag the comparison.
